title: Plan W: AI Documentary Narration
summary: Research → narration script → voice-over → visual generation → music & captions
scenario: For long-form educational videos on history, science or nature — AI brings the production cost down to a solo creator.

steps.title: Research
steps.detail: Search with Perplexity and cross-check sources, then have ChatGPT assemble a narrative spine with a clear arc and a timeline of verifiable facts. This step decides whether viewers trust you on the facts.
steps.tips: Keep source links for every key fact so you can re-check during editing and avoid embarrassing errors.

steps.title: Narration script
steps.detail: Write the voice-over chapter by chapter in conversational short sentences with strong imagery, aiming for roughly 240-280 characters per minute in Chinese, and note what each section should show on screen.
steps.tips: Outline first, then expand section by section; asking for a whole film in one pass gets you a scattered structure.

steps.title: Voice-over
steps.detail: Turn the script into a calm, storytelling narration; generate long episodes in segments and stitch them, so a flubbed line only needs one segment re-recorded.
steps.tips: Put pause and emphasis marks into the text — the documentary feel shows up immediately.

steps.title: Visual generation
steps.detail: Batch-generate atmospheric shots like historical reenactments, macro or aerial views from the shot prompts, and animate static images in Hailuo; keep real archival footage and maps for key facts.
steps.tips: Reuse a fixed 'tone + era' style prefix so the whole film looks like one piece.

steps.title: Music & captions
steps.detail: Generate ambient score and bed sounds in Suno, then overlay narration captions, title cards and chapter headings.
steps.tips: Keep the score around -18 to -20 dB so it never buries the narration.

pitfalls.title: Factual errors
pitfalls.detail: In the knowledge niche, fabricated details are fatal — verify every key fact by hand.

pitfalls.title: Narration that reads like a textbook
pitfalls.detail: Educational video should be conversational; formal writing sounds like reading aloud.

pitfalls.title: Visuals out of sync with the narration
pitfalls.detail: Write the narration first and build the visuals to match it.
